curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8854-1/ (scans; the crane is pages 4-27, the alternate model after)

functions.does: The yellow beacon on the cab roof steers the front wheels: it caps a shaft that runs down through the cab to a bevel pair, and a shaft forward to an 8-tooth gear on the rack between the steering arms.
functions.source: book: steps 4-5, 7, 14 and 20; inferred: the book draws no knob, but the beacon is the only part on top of the steering shaft

functions.does: The handwheel low on the chassis's left side slews the superstructure round on its turntable: an 8-tooth gear turns a crown gear, then an 8-tooth and 24-tooth pair, and an 8-tooth gear under the turntable turns the crown gear on the superstructure's post.
functions.source: book: steps 6-8 and 12 (the inset shows the gear on the turntable's post turning)

functions.does: The handwheel low on the chassis's right side lowers and raises both rear stabiliser legs together: a worm on its long shaft turns a 24-tooth gear, and a shaft with a universal joint and bevel gears at the back turns both legs' parallel arms.
Each stabiliser leg's foot, two pulley wheels on toothed toggle joints, tilts to sit flat on the ground.
functions.source: book: step 9 (insets 1-5); inferred: the book doesn't show it tilting

functions.does: Either handwheel at the back of the superstructure winds the winch, raising or lowering the hook: the drum is the axle between them with the string tied between two bushes, and the string runs along the boom, over the pulley at its tip, down round the hook's pulley and back up to the tip.
A ratchet holds the hook up: a pawl on a toothed toggle joint rests on the 24-tooth gear on the winch drum.
functions.source: book: step 15 (the inset shows the pawl on the gear); inferred: what it's for
functions.skip: only resists gravity; the winch handwheels work both ways without it

functions.does: The handwheel at the boom's pivot, on the right, extends and retracts the boom's grey inner section: a worm at the pivot drives two 8-tooth gears and a shaft with a universal joint along the boom to bevel gears at its tip, which drive the rack under the grey section.
functions.source: book: boom steps 4 and 7-11, main step 21; the cover shows 170 mm of travel

functions.does: The two pneumatic cylinders behind the cab raise and lower the boom: their piston rods slide out as the boom rises, and the cylinders tilt on their pivot axle.
functions.note: In the set the pump and valve work the cylinders; dragging the boom stands in for them until air is modelled.

functions.does: Pumping the spring-loaded pump on the chassis, with the valve lever on the superstructure pushed one way or the other, raises or lowers the boom.
The four wheels roll freely; nothing drives them.
The hook hangs straight down beneath the boom tip as the superstructure slews, the boom luffs and the boom extends.
functions.note: hangs under gravity; no test checks it yet

questions.question: Is the trans-yellow beacon on the cab roof the steering knob? Do the feet tilt?
